Edit here, re-run scripts/build-voice.py, and every scene's on-screen duration follows the new wav length automatically. `hold` adds on-screen seconds after the voice stops, for cards that need reading time. `lengthScale` and `sentenceSilence` set the caption reading rate — see scripts/check-pacing.py, which gates it.

scenes.text: Your backtest and your live system are usually two different codebases. That's why they drift.
You describe it once, in Rust. For example: an order book, fanned out to each side, recombined into a quote.
Under the hood it's a graph. Each node runs once per cycle, even where branches recombine.
Run it historically. Three seconds of market data replays in under half a millisecond.
Run the same graph live. Paced by the wall clock. Same values, same order. Only the clock changes.
One definition. Two run modes. The implementations can't drift.
